knowledge_base.title: Fertilizer & Nutrient Deficiency Knowledge Base

dominant_types: Medium to Deep Black Cotton Soil (Vertisols)

knowledge_base.source_authority: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Dharwad – Package of Practices

deficiency.name: Nitrogen Deficiency
symptoms: Yellowing (chlorosis) beginning from the tips of older/lower leaves
V-shaped yellow discoloration progressing up the midrib
Overall pale-green to yellow plant appearance
Stunted and spindly plant growth
Reduced tillering and poor canopy development
Early senescence of lower leaves turning brown
deficiency.visual_description: Yellow V-shaped pattern starting at leaf tip of lower leaves, moving upward along the midrib toward the base
deficiency.distinction_notes: Unlike Sulphur deficiency, N deficiency starts on older/lower leaves (mobile nutrient)

fertilizer_sources.name: Urea
fertilizer_sources.notes: Most economical; splits recommended to reduce volatilization

fertilizer_sources.name: DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate)
fertilizer_sources.notes: Used as basal, provides both N and P

fertilizer_sources.name: Ammonium Sulphate
fertilizer_sources.notes: Preferred on alkaline black soils; also supplies Sulphur

deficiency.name: Phosphorus Deficiency
symptoms: Purple or reddish-purple discoloration on undersides and margins of lower leaves
Dark green upper leaf surface with purple tinge
Slender, stiff, erect plant posture
Delayed silking and tasseling (late maturity)
Poor and shallow root system development
Reduced kernel set and poor cob development
deficiency.visual_description: Reddish-purple pigmentation (anthocyanin accumulation) on leaf margins and undersides, especially in young seedlings under cold/wet conditions
deficiency.distinction_notes: Purple coloration can also appear under cold temperatures even without deficiency; confirm with soil test

application_schedule.method: Band placement below seed, 5 cm deep

fertilizer_sources.name: DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate)
fertilizer_sources.notes: Most popular basal fertilizer in Dharwad; provides N and P together

fertilizer_sources.name: SSP (Single Super Phosphate)
fertilizer_sources.notes: Also supplies Sulphur (12%) and Calcium; preferred for Zn-deficient soils

recommendation_dharwad.critical_soil_threshold_ppm: < 10 ppm available P (Olsen's method) – Low for Dharwad soils

deficiency.name: Potassium Deficiency
symptoms: Marginal leaf burn (scorching) on tips and edges of lower/older leaves
Yellowing followed by brown necrotic edges starting at leaf tip
Weak stalks prone to lodging
Reduced stalk diameter and poor standability
Increased susceptibility to stalk rots (Fusarium, Gibberella)
Poor cob fill and light kernels
deficiency.visual_description: Brown, crispy, necrotic leaf margins and tips on older leaves progressing inward, giving a 'fired' appearance
deficiency.distinction_notes: K deficiency symptoms on margins/tips vs. N which shows V-shape along midrib

fertilizer_sources.name: MOP (Muriate of Potash / KCl)
fertilizer_sources.notes: Most common and economical; avoid on Cl-sensitive stages

fertilizer_sources.name: SOP (Sulphate of Potash)
fertilizer_sources.notes: Preferred where both K and S are needed; premium cost

deficiency.name: Zinc Deficiency
symptoms: Broad white to yellow interveinal stripes on young leaves (white bud)
White or bleached bands/stripes running lengthwise on newly emerging leaves
Stunted and rosette plant appearance
Short internodes – compressed plant height
Delayed emergence of new leaves
Poor tasseling and silking
Reduced grain number and cob length
deficiency.visual_description: Characteristic white/yellow stripes between veins on younger upper leaves; veins remain green while interveinal areas bleach out
deficiency.distinction_notes: Affects younger leaves (immobile nutrient); very common in Dharwad black cotton soils with high pH (>7.5)
deficiency.prevalence_dharwad: HIGH – One of the most widespread micronutrient deficiencies in Dharwad soils

application_schedule.method: Soil incorporation; avoid direct contact with seed
Two sprays at 25 DAS and 40 DAS

fertilizer_sources.name: Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate (ZnSO4·7H2O)
fertilizer_sources.notes: Standard recommendation; apply every 3–4 seasons if soil test shows adequacy

fertilizer_sources.name: Chelated Zinc (EDTA-Zn)
fertilizer_sources.notes: For foliar application; more efficient in alkaline conditions

recommendation_dharwad.critical_soil_threshold_ppm: < 0.6 ppm DTPA-extractable Zn – Deficient (most Dharwad Vertisols fall below this)

deficiency.name: Sulphur Deficiency
symptoms: Uniform yellowing of young/upper leaves (unlike N – starts on newer growth)
Pale green to lemon-yellow discoloration of emerging leaves
Older leaves remain green while younger leaves turn yellow
Reduced plant height and delayed maturity
Poor protein synthesis affecting grain quality
Striped chlorosis pattern on young leaves in severe cases
deficiency.visual_description: Uniform pale-yellow to lemon coloration of younger upper leaves while lower leaves remain green; no distinct stripe pattern
deficiency.distinction_notes: Key distinction: S deficiency appears on younger leaves (immobile), N on older leaves (mobile). Increasingly observed in Dharwad due to shift from SSP/AS to Urea+DAP combinations
deficiency.prevalence_dharwad: INCREASING – Sulfur deficiency has risen significantly due to widespread use of S-free fertilizers (Urea + DAP)

application_schedule.method: Soil incorporation along with other basal fertilizers

fertilizer_sources.name: Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O)
fertilizer_sources.notes: Most economical S source; also improves soil structure; preferred for Dharwad black soils

fertilizer_sources.name: SSP (Single Super Phosphate)
fertilizer_sources.notes: Simultaneously supplies P and S; excellent choice for Dharwad soils

fertilizer_sources.name: Ammonium Sulphate
fertilizer_sources.notes: Supplies both N and S; good for alkaline soils

deficiency.name: Boron Deficiency
symptoms: Death or distortion of growing point (apical meristem)
Thick, leathery, brittle leaves with wavy margins
Failure of tassel to emerge fully (tassel ear disorder)
Poor or absent silk emergence leading to barren cobs
Hollow stem at internodes (internal decay)
Short, barren cobs with poor kernel set
Brittle, discolored brace roots
deficiency.visual_description: Growing point death; younger leaves appear thick, crinkled, and fail to unfurl; tassel remains trapped or barren; silks absent or few
deficiency.distinction_notes: Critical during pollination period; B deficiency severely impacts reproductive success; common in light-textured leached soils of Dharwad red soil tracts
deficiency.prevalence_dharwad: MODERATE – More prevalent in well-leached red soils (Alfisols) than black soils in Dharwad district

application_schedule.method: Mix Borax with soil/FYM before sowing; avoid direct seed contact

application_schedule.timing: Foliar spray (if deficiency appears at V6–V8)
application_schedule.method: Two foliar sprays – at 30 DAS and at pre-tasseling (45–50 DAS)

fertilizer_sources.name: Borax (Na2B4O7·10H2O)
fertilizer_sources.notes: Standard soil application source; mix thoroughly in soil

fertilizer_sources.name: Boric Acid (H3BO3)
fertilizer_sources.notes: Better suited for foliar spray; dissolves readily in water

fertilizer_sources.name: Solubor
fertilizer_sources.notes: Highly soluble; used for foliar application especially during silking

biofertilizers.name: Azospirillum
biofertilizers.benefit: BNF – fixes 20–25 kg N/ha; reduces chemical N requirement by 10–15%

biofertilizers.name: PSB (Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria)
biofertilizers.benefit: Improves P availability; reduces chemical P requirement by 10–15%

biofertilizers.name: VAM (Vesicular-Arbuscular Mycorrhiza)
biofertilizers.benefit: Enhances Zn and P uptake in Dharwad soils

integrated_nutrient_management.soil_testing_lab: Soil Testing Laboratory, UAS Dharwad / Department of Agriculture, Dharwad

quick_reference_summary.symptoms: Yellowing from lower leaves upward; V-shaped yellow pattern along midrib
Purple-red leaf margins and undersides; delayed maturity; poor roots
Brown scorching on leaf margins and tips; weak stalks; lodging
White/yellow interveinal stripes on young leaves; white bud; stunted growth
Uniform yellowing of young upper leaves; older leaves remain green
Growing point death; poor silking/tasseling; hollow stem; barren cobs
